Summary

Data-source overview:  
The blog-style year-in-review text contains brief references to several AI-safety research projects: the AI Safety Gridworlds paper (studying specification gaming), the Reward-Corruption in RL paper, and a public talk on interpretability for AI safety. Although the post does not describe the projects in depth, it clearly flags the risks they tackle and the solutions they propose. Using moderate inference, an integrated knowledge fabric was constructed that links the three research strands into one connected graph from a shared top-level risk, through problems, insights, design rationales, mechanisms and evidence, to three actionable interventions.

Extraction confidence[68]  
The source mentions only project titles, so substantial but careful inference (edge confidence 2) was required to fill in missing details. The JSON passes all structural checks and every node is connected, but precision is limited by the terse source.

Inference strategy justification  
Information explicitly present (project titles) was mapped to their well-known public contents (e.g. Gridworlds ⇒ specification-gaming experiments). Only standard, widely cited claims from those works were inferred, marked with confidence 2. This keeps the graph faithful while still delivering complete risk-to-intervention pathways.

Extraction completeness explanation  
All three AI-safety research items in the source are represented. Each produces a full path (risk → problem analysis → theoretical insight → design rationale → implementation mechanism → validation evidence → intervention). Paths interconnect at the common risk node, yielding one coherent fabric with 19 nodes and 24 edges; no isolated components remain.

Key limitations  
1. Edge evidence is mostly “medium/weak” because the paper contents had to be inferred.  
2. Fine-grained numerical results had to be omitted; they were not in the blog post.  
3. Section titles in the post are informal; “Research/career” was treated as the closest heading for most AI-safety references.
